messages:
sam: Hey @support — after upgrading our prod workers to py-sdk 1.30.0 we started getting an exception when calling client.generate: 
TypeError: generate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'stop'
Rolling back to 1.29.4 fixed it immediately. Anybody seen this? We hit this in a canary and paused deploy.

deploy-bot: Published redwood-inference 1.30.0 to PyPI (artifact: redwood-inference-1.30.0.whl) :package:  
elaine: thanks for the ping — can you paste a minimal repro + pip freeze? Also any request_id from the failed calls would help.

sam: repro below (minimal):
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
resp = client.generate(model="open-1", prompt="hi", stop=['\n'])
print(resp)
```
pip freeze: `redwood-inference==1.30.0` + normal deps. Error trace: `TypeError: generate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'stop'`

jordan: I can reproduce with that snippet on 1.30.0. Looks like in 1.30 we removed the legacy alias `stop` in favor of `stop_sequences` (internal rename) but we didn't keep a compatibility shim or emit a DeprecationWarning — that's a bug. I'll escalate.

jordan: short-term workaround: pin to 1.29.4 in your deploys: `pip install redwood-inference==1.29.4` or add a compatibility call: `resp = client.generate(..., stop_sequences=...)`.

sam: pin worked, thanks. Can you confirm whether 1.30 also changed retry semantics? We saw one duplicate response in logs and worried about double billing.

jordan: good question. 1.30 didn't intentionally change server-side idempotency, but there was a client-side refactor that touched the retry wrapper — we've seen one case where retries triggered without propagating the idempotency header in rare async flows. Please send one sample request_id from the duplicate so we can correlate.

sam: attaching two request_ids: `req_01FXXXA` and `req_01FYYYB`. Also pasting the small log snippet where we saw the second call: `INFO request_id=req_01FYYYB retry=1 status=200 token_cost=12`

elaine: escalating to eng-sre/eng-runtime. Jordan, can you open an internal ticket with repro and the two request_ids? We'll add the user to the incident trace if needed.

jordan: created REDWOOD-4218: "py-sdk 1.30 compat regression: removed legacy stop alias and rare retry idempotency drop" — assigning to eng-runtime. Putting a high-priority label. Owner: @jordan.

jordan: proposed fix: restore a compatibility shim that accepts `stop` and emits DeprecationWarning, plus a test that verifies idempotency header flows through async retry wrapper. If tests pass, cut 1.30.1 patch. ETA: hoping for same-day patch, depending on CI.

devex-bot: Migration note queued: docs/migration/python.md updated with `stop -> stop_sequences` and pin guidance. Also added note about checking idempotency headers after upgrade.

sam: appreciate the quick turnaround. One more question — what pin range should we recommend to our SREs? I don't want minor bumps to auto-upgrade.

elaine: recommend pinning to `redwood-inference==1.29.4` until 1.30.1 is published and validated. If you must accept 1.30.x, use a strict upper bound in your constraints: `redwood-inference>=1.30.0,<1.30.1` while we validate the patch.

jordan: update: we've reproduced the idempotency repro locally, fixed the header propagation in the async retry wrapper, added a unit/integration test, and ran CI. If green, we'll release 1.30.1 with the compatibility shim and the retry fix.

sam: confirmed 1.30.1 (we tested a canary build) — compatibility shim worked and no duplicate billing traces in our short smoke tests. :thumbsup:

elaine: closing loop here — please re-open if you see anything else. We'll follow up with a changelog entry and public migration note.

sam: thanks everyone — saved our deploy window.
